column1: # clues.tsv for ft_abs.h — hints only, never answers.

ABS(x) must give the absolute value. A macro body is pasted in where an expression is expected, so it cannot contain statements such as if: which C operators choose between two values inside one expression? What should it produce for a positive number, a negative number, and zero?

The argument can be an EXPRESSION such as 2 - 5, not just a plain number. Write out by hand what ABS(2 - 5) becomes once the preprocessor has pasted it into your body, then evaluate that text the way C would, operator by operator. Is the result what you meant?

Your macro is also dropped INSIDE a bigger expression. Write out by hand what 2 * ABS(-3) becomes after substitution, then evaluate it the way C would: which operator is applied first? Does the text still mean "twice the absolute value of -3"?
